turns.user_message: Hola, tengo una cita la semana que viene pero estoy con fiebre, prefiero cancelarla.
turns.agent_response: Lo siento, tuve un problema técnico. ¿Puedes intentarlo de nuevo? 💕

bugs.detail: manage_appointments EXECUTED the cancel successfully (cancellation_service logged 'Appointment e72251cb cancelled by customer', customer_id 69a15c4e was present — NO CUSTOMER_ID_REQUIRED), but the graph invocation then crashed in the Redis checkpointer with 'TypeError: Type is not JSON serializable: asyncpg.pgproto.pgproto.UUID' at langgraph/checkpoint/redis/base.py:_msgpack_to_redis_json (orjson.dumps). The resolved customer_id is persisted to graph state as a raw asyncpg.pgproto.pgproto.UUID (likely via the O2 ExtendedModelResponse + Command path) instead of a str / stdlib uuid.UUID, which orjson cannot serialize. The agent fell back to the generic error message and never persisted the checkpoint.
bugs.evidence: agent logs 2026-06-10T11:02:29 (cancel ok) -> 2026-06-10T11:02:32 (TypeError checkpoint save failure) -> fallback message sent

turns.agent_response:
¡Hola! Soy Maite, asistenta virtual con IA de Atrévete 🌸

No veo ninguna cita programada ahora mismo, así que no hay nada que cancelar.

Si quieres, puedo ayudarte a comprobar si era para otra fecha o con otro nombre.

bugs.detail: Because turn 1's checkpoint never persisted (has_checkpoint=false), turn 2 starts from an empty state: the disclosure replays the full 'Soy Maite...' first-contact greeting, and the bot has no memory of the just-executed cancellation. It correctly reports no active appointment (the DB row is already cancelled) but cannot confirm the cancellation it performed one turn earlier.

Redis checkpointer cannot serialize the resolved customer_id stored as asyncpg.pgproto.pgproto.UUID. The cancel side-effect commits to the DB, but no checkpoint is saved and the user receives a generic technical-error message instead of a cancel confirmation. Regression introduced/exposed by the Change O2 customer_id persistence path. Fix: convert the resolved customer_id to str (or stdlib uuid.UUID) before writing it to AgentState / the Command update.
Downstream of the checkpoint crash: every turn restarts with no conversation history (has_checkpoint=false).

passed_note: DB-truth outcome matches expected (status=cancelled, manage_appointments fired, no forbidden tool calls, N4 held, O2 customer_id fix confirmed). HOWEVER a CRITICAL infra regression (asyncpg.UUID checkpoint serialization crash) broke the user-facing turn: the user got a technical-error message instead of a cancel confirmation and the checkpoint was lost. The transaction succeeded but the conversation UX failed.
